From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Reserved capacity ask and price-protection question

Jordan — ran the numbers and attached a short model (gpu_sensitivity_model.xlsx). Summary:

- Base case (no GPU price movement): 20% discount at 1.2M hours yields ~22% gross margin on Dedicated capacity.
- Downside scenario (GPU spot market up 30%): margin compresses to ~6% for the same discount band.
- At 30% effective discount requested by Acuity, downside margin goes negative under >25% GPU price inflation.

Options to make a 30% effective discount sustainable:
1) Staggered activation: 40% of capacity in year 1, 60% in year 2 (reduces exposure to immediate market shocks).
2) GPU price collar: we absorb up to +10% GPU inflation; beyond that, price pass-through or credit mechanism kicks in.
3) Shorten firm commit to 18 months with an option to extend if GPU cost stabilizes.

If Jordan wants to offer an exceptional discount (>=30%) we'll need Exec approval from Sales leadership and finance sign-off. Ben/Marissa — tagging you for quick read and approvals path.

Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: gpu_sensitivity_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) --

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Reserved capacity ask and price-protection question

Quick legal/ops note:

- Indexation clauses: acceptable from an ops perspective if tied to a published, auditable index (we should avoid vendor-specific SPOT references). Indexation requires monthly reconciliation and an ops SLA trigger for capacity rebalancing.
- Price collar: workable but needs explicit definitions for measurement window, cap threshold, and remediation (credits vs. pass-through).
- Contract tenor: 24 months is long — propose an 18+6 structure (18-month firm, 6-month optional extension) with a re-price window at month 12 if market moves >20%.

Also recommend adding a modest annualized cap on unusual pass-throughs and a defined dispute window to prevent billing surprises.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

- Deal: Acuity Labs — 1.2M GPU hours, requested 24-month tenor.
- Their target: ~30% effective discount off list. Marcus' model shows that a 30% discount would put us at negative-to-low margins under a >25% GPU price spike.

If approved, I will finalize the term sheet with Acuity and include the indexation/pass-through language Olga recommended. Time is tight — Samira asked for the next iteration by EOD Friday.

Jordan/Ben — after reviewing Marcus' sensitivity and Olga's constraints, I approve the conditional structure with the following terms:

1) Offer up to 30% effective discount but only under a formal 18+6 tenor (18 firm, 6 optional), with staggered activation: 40% year 1, 60% year 2.
2) Insert a GPU price collar: Redwood absorbs up to +10% GPU cost movement measured on a 60-day rolling window; beyond that an agreed pass-through applies.
3) Include an annual true-up and a mid-term reprice trigger at month 12 if cumulative price movement >20%.
4) Require Acuity to accept a modest non-refundable first tranche deposit to secure the activation schedule.

Jordan — you have approval to present this as the final commercial offer. Work with Olga to lock the legal language around indexation/collar and with Marcus to ensure the invoice cadence and accounting treatment are clear.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
